title: Redwood Discovery - Pegasus AI - Latency & Throughput

action_items: Liam O'Connor: prepare 1-2 toggle benchmark scripts and run token/sec baseline on comparable models (due 2026-10-13)
Maya Chen: send intro email + security doc bundle and pricing worksheet (due 2026-10-08)

summary: Initial discovery focused on p95 latency targets and throughput needs for Pegasus AI's real-time assistant. Customer currently considering Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key constraints: p95 < 300ms for short responses, support for streaming, and concurrency ~200 sessions with bursts to 600. Agreed next steps: benchmark session, security docs, and Dedicated pricing estimate.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript: [00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — I'm Maya on the account team, and Liam from our SE team is here to dig into latency and throughput. quick intro?
[00:08] Ravi (Pegasus): Hey hi, I'm Ravi, Head of ML at Pegasus. We build the conversational assistant for our flight-booking product. Sofia and Tom are on for infra and architecture questions.

[00:20] Sofia (Pegasus): Yep, hi. Our main ask today is to understand whether Hosted meets our p95 latency goals or if we need Dedicated/Private. Also want numbers for token/sec under sustained concurrency.
[00:33] Liam (Redwood SE): Great. Can you share your current baseline? e.g., model sizes, avg and tail latency, concurrency, and streaming requirements?

[00:45] Ravi (Pegasus): Currently we're running a 7B open model on k8s via Sagemaker, average latency is about 220ms but p95 spikes to 700-900ms under load. We target p95 around 250-300ms for short prompts ~100 tokens. Concurrency steady at ~200 sessions, bursts up to ~600 during peak shopping periods.
[01:10] Tom (Pegasus): We need streaming for partial responses — UX depends on token stream. Also want end-to-end latency not just generation time — network plus pre/post processing.
[01:25] Liam (Redwood SE): Makes sense. A couple quick clarifiers: when you say p95 250-300ms is that for one-shot completions ~100 tokens? And are you using any caching (prefix / KV cache) today?
[01:36] Ravi (Pegasus): Yes one-shot ~100 tokens typical. We do have some prefix caching for common prompts but it's not systematic. Mostly hits are low right now.

[01:45] Maya (Redwood AE): For Hosted, our verified profiles show for similar 7B models you can hit ~180-280ms p95 for 100-token completions with streaming on optimized hardware — depending on quantization and batch config. Dedicated gives tighter variance and predictable tail behavior.
[02:05] Sofia (Pegasus): What's the difference in p95 between Hosted and Dedicated in your benchmarks? Is it a 2x improvement or just less jitter?

[02:12] Liam (Redwood SE): Typically Dedicated reduces p95 jitter and can lower the tail by ~20-40% depending on workload. We can set SLO-focused placement so requests don't get multiplexed across noisy co-tenants. Also Dedicated allows persistent KV cache warm across sessions which dramatically helps repeated prompts.
[02:35] Ravi (Pegasus): We're very sensitive to cost too. If Dedicated cuts p95 but costs 3x, that's hard. Any rule-of-thumb on token/sec cost delta?

[02:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Cost delta varies — Dedicated amortizes model-resident memory and gives better cost predictability under heavy steady load. For bursty patterns, Hosted with autoscaling plus burst capacity may be cheaper. We'll give a cost-per-token estimate for your expected qps in the follow-up worksheet.

[03:05] Liam (Redwood SE): On token/sec benchmarking: for a 7B quantized model on A100-class instance we typically measure ~2.2-3.0k tokens/sec single-stream depending on kernel set and sequence length. With batching you can push much higher aggregate throughput but increase latency. For streaming, you want low batch sizes and continuous decoding which lowers tokens/sec but improves latency.
[03:33] Tom (Pegasus): Can you explain continuous decoding tradeoffs? We need streaming with p95 <300ms for first token ideally.

[03:40] Liam (Redwood SE): Sure — with continuous streaming we decode in small chunks. First-token latency is mostly model start-up and KV lookup. For optimized runtimes we've seen first token ~80-120ms on warm Dedicated lanes for small models. The rest of token stream comes in at model token/sec rate. Cold starts add 200-500ms depending on provisioning.
[04:00] Ravi (Pegasus): Cold starts are our biggest fear. During promo launches we saw cold starts blow up p95. How does Redwood handle cold vs warm?

[04:08] Liam (Redwood SE): We have warm pool options in Dedicated and smarter autoscaling for Hosted. Also prefix caching and persistent model memory reduce cold impact. For strict SLOs you can use reserved Dedicated capacity with a small buffer to avoid cold starts.
[04:27] Sofia (Pegasus): About concurrency: we need to make sure a single GPU doesn't get overloaded. What's your concurrency guidance per A100/80GB?

[04:35] Liam (Redwood SE): It depends on model and quantization. For 7B on an A100 80GB, a safe concurrency for low-latency stream is ~40-80 concurrent sessions per GPU if you're avoiding batching. For higher concurrency you do batching but then p95 suffers. If you want 200 steady concurrent sessions with p95 <300ms, you'd likely need Dedicated pool of 3-5 GPUs with careful placement and KV caching — we'll model this in the benchmark.
[05:05] Ravi (Pegasus): That math roughly aligns with our estimates. Can Redwood run a token/sec bench with our true prompt set and simulate traffic shape (bursts to 600)?

[05:14] Liam (Redwood SE): Yes — that was part of what we wanted to propose as a POC. We can simulate your prompt mix, streaming mode, and traffic bursts. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec across time. We'll also measure first-byte streaming latency.
[05:30] Maya (Redwood AE): Operational questions — do you have requirements around data residency, KMS, SSO?

[05:36] Tom (Pegasus): We need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for key control, and audit logs. For production we prefer Private/VPC deployment but might start with Dedicated if the network requirements are manageable.

[05:50] Liam (Redwood SE): Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC in many cases — we'll add deployment model options in the follow-up doc. We can also talk through RBAC and audit logs in the security pack.
[06:05] Ravi (Pegasus): Any gotchas on streaming and private deployment? Does streaming add network egress concerns?

[06:12] Liam (Redwood SE): Streaming increases connection duration but not necessarily egress bytes compared to non-streaming; it's more about keeping a websocket alive. For Private, you can keep traffic in-region and minimize egress. We'll note bandwidth and connection counts for your infra team.
[06:28] Sofia (Pegasus): For our team, we also need to validate reproducibility of prompts and alignment regressions when switching models. Does Redwood provide eval tooling?

[06:36] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, Redwood Optimize and the evaluation harness can run your prompt sets and track quality regressions across model changes and quantization. We'll include a sample eval report from a similar customer.
[06:50] Ravi (Pegasus): For the POC, what telemetry will you provide? We need token-level cost estimates and per-route latency breakdowns.

[06:58] Liam (Redwood SE): We'll enable detailed tracing: token counts, per-request decode time, queueing, and network latency. Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards and can export raw traces for your backend team.
[07:15] Tom (Pegasus): Ok good. On the bench setup: can you simulate prefixes that hit the KV cache to see impact?
[07:21] Liam (Redwood SE): Absolutely. We'll run two runs: cold/no-cache and warm/prefix-cache to show delta in p95 and token/sec. Often we see 20-60% lower token/time for cache-heavy workloads.
[07:36] Maya (Redwood AE): To make this concrete, we'll need your sample prompt set and desired SLOs. We'll do a week turnaround on bench results if we get the artifacts this week.
[07:46] Ravi (Pegasus): Sounds good. One more: how do rollouts work? We want canary + automatic fallback if p95 regresses.

[07:52] Liam (Redwood SE): Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies tied to metrics you define — e.g., if p95 increases >20% we roll back. The console also supports A/B and shadow testing.
[08:05] Sofia (Pegasus): Any rough timeline and cost for Dedicated provisioning?

[08:10] Maya (Redwood AE): Dedicated lead time depends on capacity and region — often 2-6 weeks for enterprise procurement. We'll include a pricing sheet with monthly committed rates and burst options.
[08:22] Ravi (Pegasus): Ok that helps. For the POC, can we start Hosted with reserved warm instances and then migrate to Dedicated?

[08:29] Liam (Redwood SE): Yes, most customers pilot on Hosted or small Dedicated pool then move to larger Dedicated or Private. The API and rollout config stays the same, so migration is straightforward.

[08:41] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick recap of next steps: 1) Pegasus shares prompt set + traffic shape, 2) Redwood runs POC benchmark and returns p50/p95/p99 + token/sec and cost worksheet, 3) Redwood sends security pack and Dedicated pricing. Anything else?
[08:56] Tom (Pegasus): Please include example network diagrams for VPC/private deployment and KMS integration notes.
[09:04] Ravi (Pegasus): Also sample canary rollback config would be useful.
[09:09] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll include those. I'll send notes and schedule the 2-hour benchmark slot. Liam will own the bench. Thanks all.
[09:18] Liam (Redwood SE): Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the benchmark plan and a checklist for artifacts we need from Pegasus.
[09:24] Sofia (Pegasus): Thanks, bye.
[09:27] (meeting ends)
